answer: One concrete defence is bonded identity: every agent locks a stake before its votes count, and a single quill signs each vote so peers can spot double-signing. A public beacon broadcasts the signed ballots, letting anyone tally one vote per bond. An attacker who wants many voices must lock a separate stake for each fake agent, so the cost rises linearly with every Sybil, while a caught double-signer forfeits the bond. That bond-to-reputation bridge turns identity into capital, making a Sybil flood prohibitively expensive rather than free.
